why: A repository importing a library that is another declared repository. Without the join `billing` holds an external placeholder for `shared.money.to_cents` and the call disappears at the repository edge — so "who calls this" answers with the library's own repo only, and a breaking change to it looks safe. `json` is the control: also external, genuinely third-party, and must stay a placeholder. A joiner that repointed every external import would pass on `shared` and destroy this.
excluded: `py:shared.money.to_cents` as an external placeholder is deliberately absent: after the join it must not exist, and the IMPORTS and CALLS that referenced it must both have moved to the real function. Moving only the import would drop a real call edge when the placeholder is removed — a join that destroys knowledge instead of adding it.
